violations.message: RiskReport must link at least one evidence id.

input_narrative: SYNTHETIC NARRATIVE: Synthetic remote monitoring center reported that the device failed to flag a clinically significant complete atrioventricular block episode in real time. A retrospective clinician review confirms a single missed, sustained complete atrioventricular block episode that self-resolved with no recorded adverse outcome; no second occurrence has yet been confirmed. The device's own confidence-score log and the clinician's retrospective read disagree on episode duration, an unresolved discrepancy.

The discrepancy between the device’s confidence score log (ARTIFACT-TESTLOG-2025A, ARTIFACT-TESTLOG-2029A) and clinician review raises concerns about algorithm performance or data interpretation. This requires investigation to determine root cause and prevent recurrence. risk_report.rationale: A clinically significant complete atrioventricular block episode was missed by the device's real-time monitoring system, confirmed by retrospective clinician review. While the event self-resolved without recorded adverse outcome and no recurrence has been confirmed, a missed detection of this type represents a serious potential patient safety risk, particularly given that it is a safety-critical function. The discrepancy between the device’s confidence score log (ARTIFACT-TESTLOG-2025A, ARTIFACT-TESTLOG-2029A) and clinician review raises concerns about algorithm performance or data interpretation. This requires investigation to determine root cause and prevent recurrence.  The EU MDR mandates that devices with electronic programmable systems are designed to ensure repeatability, reliability, and performance (mdr-annexI-sec17.1), and that appropriate means be adopted to eliminate or reduce risks in the event of a single fault condition (mdr-annexI-sec17.2).  Furthermore, 21 CFR § 820.10(c) requires design controls for devices automated with computer software.
